name: Kansas
agency: Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night (25 before a restricted license at 15; affidavit of the full 50 before 16). Driver education hours do not count.
teen.nightLimit: Restricted license at 16: may drive alone 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., plus work, school activities and religious services. At 15: only to/from work, to/from school on school days by the most direct route, and religious activities 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.; any time with a licensed adult 21+ in the front seat.
teen.passengerLimit: Under 16: no non-sibling minor passengers. At 16, first six months: no more than one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family.
teen.phone: Permit and restricted license holders: no wireless communication device while driving except to report illegal activity or summon medical or emergency help. All drivers: texting ban (K.S.A. 8-15,111).

notes: Permit: supervising licensed adult at least 21 in the front seat; no one else in the front seat (KDOR GDL page).
Knowledge test: commercial sites say 25 questions, 20 correct (80 percent); not confirmed on an official page, so exam fields are null. Spanish test availability not confirmed.
Restricted license at 15 requires an approved driver education course. If the 50-hour affidavit is not provided, restrictions continue until 17 (KDOR FAQ).
Speed (K.S.A. 8-1558): 75 mph on designated, posted separated multilane highways; 55 on county or township highways; 65 on other highways.
Stop for a stopped school bus, church bus or day care bus loading children; opposing traffic on a divided highway need not stop (handbook; K.S.A. 8-1556).
Seat belts: primary enforcement for driver and front-seat passenger since June 2010 (KHP).
Move over: SB 8, in effect July 1, 2025, extends the law to any stationary vehicle showing hazard warning lights; change lanes if possible, otherwise slow down (news sources, statute text not read).
